H1121: a son (as a builder of the family name), in the widest sense (of literal and figurative relationship, including grandson, subject, nation, quality or condition, etc., (like father or brother), etc.)
H4148: properly, chastisement; figuratively, reproof, warning or instruction; also restraint
H1: father, in a literal and immediate, or figurative and remote application
H3887: properly, to make mouths at, i.e. to scoff; hence (from the effort to pronounce a foreign language) to interpret, or (generally) intercede
H3808: not (the simple or abs. negation); by implication, no; often used with other particles
H8085: to hear intelligently (often with implication of attention, obedience, etc.; causatively, to tell, etc.)
H6310: the mouth (as the means of blowing), whether literal or figurative (particularly speech); specifically edge, portion or side; adverbially (with preposition) according to
H376: a man as an individual or a male person; often used as an adjunct to a more definite term (and in such cases frequently not expressed in translation)
H2896: good (as an adjective) in the widest sense; used likewise as a noun, both in the masculine and the feminine, the singular and the plural (good, a good or good thing, a good man or woman; the good, goods or good things, good men or women), also as an adverb (well)
H5315: properly, a breathing creature, i.e. animal of (abstractly) vitality; used very widely in a literal, accommodated or figurative sense (bodily or mental)
H898: to cover (with a garment); figuratively, to act covertly; by implication, to pillage
H2555: violence; by implication, wrong; by meton. unjust gain
H5341: to guard, in a good sense (to protect, maintain, obey, etc.) or a bad one (to conceal, etc.)
H8104: properly, to hedge about (as with thorns), i.e. guard; generally, to protect, attend to, etc.
H6589: to dispart (the feet or lips), i.e. become licentious
H8193: the lip (as a natural boundary); by implication, language; by analogy, a margin (of a vessel, water, cloth, etc.)
H4288: properly, a dissolution; concretely, a ruin, or (abstractly) consternation
H369: a non-entity; generally used as a negative particle
H2742: properly, incised or (active) incisive; hence (as noun masculine or feminine) a trench (as dug), gold (as mined), a threshing-sledge (having sharp teeth); (figuratively) determination; also eager
H1878: to be fat; transitively, to fatten (or regard as fat); specifically to anoint; figuratively, to satisfy; to remove (fat) ashes (of sacrifices)
H1697: a word; by implication, a matter (as spoken of) or thing; adverbially, a cause
H8267: an untruth; by implication, a sham (often adverbial)
H7563: morally wrong; concretely, an (actively) bad person
H887: to smell bad; figuratively, to be offensive morally
H2659: to blush; figuratively, to be ashamed, disappointed; causatively, to shame, reproach
H6666: rightness (abstractly), subjectively (rectitude), objectively (justice), morally (virtue) or figuratively (prosperity)
H1870: a road (as trodden); figuratively, a course of life or mode of action, often adverb
H5557: properly, to wrench, i.e. (figuratively) to subvert
H2403: an offence (sometimes habitual sinfulness), and its penalty, occasion, sacrifice, or expiation; also (concretely) an offender
H3426: there is or are (or any other form of the verb to be, as may suit the connection)
H6238: properly, to accumulate; chiefly (specifically) to grow (causatively, make) rich
H3605: properly, the whole; hence, all, any or every (in the singular only, but often in a plural sense)
H7227: abundant (in quantity, size, age, number, rank, quality)

H216: illumination or (concrete) luminary (in every sense, including lightning, happiness, etc.)
H8055: probably to brighten up, i.e. (figuratively) be (causatively, make) blithe or gleesome
H5216: a lamp (i.e. the burner) or light (literally or figuratively)
H1846: to be extinguished; figuratively, to expire or be dried up
H7535: properly, leanness, i.e. (figuratively) limitation; only adverbial, merely, or conjunctional, although
H5414: to give, used with greatest latitude of application (put, make, etc.)
H854: properly, nearness (used only as a preposition or an adverb), near; hence, generally, with, by, at, among, etc.
H3289: to advise; reflexively, to deliberate or resolve
H1892: emptiness or vanity; figuratively, something transitory and unsatisfactory; often used as an adverb
H4591: properly, to pare off, i.e. lessen; intransitively, to be (or causatively, to make) small or few (or figuratively, ineffective)
H5921: above, over, upon, or against (yet always in this last relation with a downward aspect) in a great variety of applications
H3027: a hand (the open one (indicating power, means, direction, etc.),
H4900: to draw, used in a great variety of applications (including to sow, to sound, to prolong, to develop, to march, to remove, to delay, to be tall, etc.)
H2470: properly, to be rubbed or worn; hence (figuratively) to be weak, sick, afflicted; or (causatively) to grieve, make sick; also to stroke (in flattering), entreat
H3820: the heart; also used (figuratively) very widely for the feelings, the will and even the intellect; likewise for the centre of anything
H6086: a tree (from its firmness); hence, wood (plural sticks)
H2416: alive; hence, raw (flesh); fresh (plant, water, year), strong; also (as noun, especially in the feminine singular and masculine plural) life (or living thing), whether literally or figuratively
H8378: a longing; by implication, a delight (subjectively, satisfaction, objectively, a charm)
H935: to go or come (in a wide variety of applications)
H2254: to wind tightly (as a rope), i.e. to bind; specifically, by a pledge; figuratively, to pervert, destroy; also to writhe in pain (especially of parturition)
H4687: a command, whether human or divine (collectively, the Law)
H1931: he (she or it); only expressed when emphatic or without a verb; also (intensively) self, or (especially with the article) the same; sometimes (as demonstrative) this or that; occasionally (instead of copula) as or are
H7999: to be safe (in mind, body or estate); figuratively, to be (causatively, make) completed; by implication, to be friendly; by extension, to reciprocate (in various applications)
H8451: a precept or statute, especially the Decalogue or Pentateuch
H4726: properly, something dug, i.e. a (general) source (of water, even when naturally flowing; also of tears, blood (by euphemism, of the female pudenda); figuratively, of happiness, wisdom, progeny)
H4170: a noose (for catching animals) (literally or figuratively); by implication, a hook (for the nose)
H4194: death (natural or violent); concretely, the dead, their place or state (hades); figuratively, pestilence, ruin
H2580: graciousness, i.e. subjective (kindness, favor) or objective (beauty)
H386: permanence; hence (concrete) permanent; specifically a chieftain
H6213: to do or make, in the broadest sense and widest application
H3684: properly, fat, i.e. (figuratively) stupid or silly
H4397: a messenger; specifically, of God, i.e. an angel (also a prophet, priest or teacher)
H5307: to fall, in a great variety of applications (intransitive or causative, literal or figurative)
H7451: bad or (as noun) evil (natural or moral)
H6735: a hinge (as pressed in turning); also a throe (as a phys. or mental pressure); also a herald or erranddoer (as constrained by the principal)
H4832: properly, curative, i.e. literally (concretely) a medicine, or (abstractly) a cure; figuratively (concretely) deliverance, or (abstractly) placidity
H6544: to loosen; by implication, to expose, dismiss; figuratively, absolve, begin
H8433: chastisement; figuratively (by words) correction, refutation, proof (even in defence)
H3513: to be heavy, i.e. in a bad sense (burdensome, severe, dull) or in a good sense (numerous, rich, honorable; causatively, to make weighty (in the same two senses)
H1961: to exist, i.e. be or become, come to pass (always emphatic, and not a mere copula or auxiliary)
H8441: properly, something disgusting (morally), i.e. (as noun) an abhorrence; especially idolatry or (concretely) an idol
H1980: to walk (in a great variety of applications, literally and figuratively)
H2449: to be wise (in mind, word or act)
H7462: to tend a flock; i.e. pasture it; intransitively, to graze (literally or figuratively); generally to rule; by extension, to associate with (as a friend)
H7489: properly, to spoil (literally, by breaking to pieces); figuratively, to make (or be) good fornothing, i.e. bad (physically, socially or morally)
H2400: a criminal, or one accounted guilty
H7291: to run after (usually with hostile intent; figuratively (of time) gone by)
H853: properly, self (but generally used to point out more definitely the object of a verb or preposition, even or namely)
H5157: to inherit (as a (figurative) mode of descent), or (generally) to occupy; causatively, to bequeath, or (generally) distribute, instate
H6845: to hide (by covering over); by implication, to hoard or reserve; figuratively to deny; specifically (favorably) to protect, (unfavorably) to lurk
H2428: probably a force, whether of men, means or other resources; an army, wealth, virtue, valor, strength
H2398: properly, to miss; hence (figuratively and generally) to sin; by inference, to forfeit, lack, expiate, repent, (causatively) lead astray, condemn
H5215: properly, plowing, i.e. (concretely) freshly plowed land
H5595: properly, to scrape (literally, to shave; but usually figuratively) together (i.e. to accumulate or increase) or away (i.e. to scatter, remove, or ruin; intransitively, to perish)
H4941: properly, a verdict (favorable or unfavorable) pronounced judicially, especially a sentence or formal decree (human or (participant's) divine law, individual or collective), including the act, the place, the suit, the crime, and the penalty; abstractly, justice, including a participant's right or privilege (statutory or customary), or even a style
H2820: to restrain or (reflex.) refrain; by implication, to refuse, spare, preserve; to observe
H7626: a scion, i.e. (literally) a stick (for punishing, writing, fighting, ruling, walking, etc.) or (figuratively) a clan
H157: to have affection for (sexually or otherwise)
H7836: properly, to dawn, i.e. (figuratively) be (up) early at any task (with the implication of earnestness); by extension, to search for (with painstaking)
H990: the belly, especially the womb; also the bosom or body of anything
H2637: to lack; by implication, to fail, want, lessen
